data.narrative:
Altara operates in the AI & Software sector at an undisclosed stage. The comparable universe consists of one public peer (Palantir Technologies, ticker PLTR) and eight private peers including Palantir, Waymo, Figure AI, Scale AI, and Reflection AI. This modest peer set reflects the nascent and heterogeneous nature of frontier AI ventures.

The peer-median method is inapplicable here. Despite identifying 16 same-sector peers within AI & Software, none satisfy the narrow filters required for a robust triangulation—specifically, no peers matched on both stage and valuation tier simultaneously. Deploying an all-sector median would introduce excessive noise and obscure company-specific drivers.

Without viable comparable company methods, this valuation exercise cannot proceed to a quantitative synthesis at this time. A credible range would require either additional stage-specific or tier-specific private transaction data, or disclosure of Altara's fundraising history and current metrics (revenue, user counts, or capital deployed) to anchor relative valuations against the public and private peer set. The key uncertainty is the absence of granular financial or operational metrics; any forward valuation must await either a narrower peer cohort or proprietary company data.
